A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TreeG research, with matching title, authors, framework, and retained experiments. All 22 pages of v1 and 34 pages of v2, including their appendices, provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures sufficient for comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original TreeG experiments on symbolic music, small molecules, and enhancer DNA, including scaling studies and ablations. Some baseline scores are explicitly borrowed, but the TreeG results are original.

after.justification: v2 retains original TreeG experiments and adds molecular optimization results, baseline comparisons, diversity measurements, and a selection-strategy ablation in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 expands selection from top-A ranking to ranking or value-weighted resampling. Value Function 1 changes from averaging fy to averaging exp(fy), which can change candidate rankings with multiple Monte Carlo samples. Module 2 also introduces a tunable next-state covariance parameter. These materially revise the reported procedure while retaining the three TreeG variants.

E1.justification: Molecular evaluation replaces lipophilicity target matching with QED, synthetic-accessibility, and DRD2 maximization, while retaining ring-count targeting. These introduce different optimization tasks within the molecule domain. Music datasets and tasks and the eight DNA cell types remain; DNA Classes 1 and 3 are relabeled, not new populations.

E2.justification: v2 evaluates TDS in the music comparison and SVDD in music, molecule, and DNA comparisons, substantially expanding the comparator set. Figure 2 removes the earlier guidance-baseline points. TreeG-G and TreeG-SD appearing in the main molecule table are not new comparators: both already appeared in v1's appendix.

E3.justification: Molecule evaluation replaces validity with Tanimoto similarity, and DNA evaluation adds pairwise Hamming-distance diversity. The main molecule comparison changes TreeG-SC from K=2, N=30 to K=4, N=10. New protocols include 500 samples for molecular maximization, four particles for music TDS, and ranking/resampling comparisons with specified temperatures and sample counts. These are reported setting changes, not evidence that every retained experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix H.3 and Table 18 add a controlled comparison of ranking against resampling at two temperatures for TreeG-SC and TreeG-SD. Existing iteration-count, Taylor-approximation, and Monte Carlo-size ablations remain, with diversity replacing validity in the discrete tests. The ring-count distribution diagnostic in v1 Figure 6 is removed; many scaling plots are retained or redisplayed.

E5.justification: Both versions retain mean-plus-dispersion reporting and the explicit definition of music losses as mean and standard deviation across 200 targets; neither adds repeated-run or seed information. However, v1 Table 9 reports uncertainties for the full music scaling grid, whereas v2 retains unbanded scaling plots and only a frontier table. This reduces uncertainty reporting for retained scaling results.

E6.justification: v2 adds optimization, diversity, baseline, and selection-ablation results and removes LogP and validity entries. Main-table TreeG-SC ring-count MAE at target 1 changes from 0.03±0.26 to 0.01±0.07 under changed K and N, so this is not a same-setting gain. The reported music frontier loss at 251.9 seconds changes from 0.057±0.179 to 0.048±0.198. Existing main music scores and DNA probability/FBD scores remain after matching the reordered cell classes.

T1.justification: v1 contains a transition-decomposition lemma but no conditional-transition approximation theorems. v2 adds Theorems 1 and 2, finite-sample bounds, explicit perfect-model assumptions, and extensive proofs and auxiliary lemmas in Appendix D. The guarantees concern A=1 resampling, with Gaussian-data/linear-objective assumptions for continuous models and bounded-likelihood conditions for discrete models.

C1.justification: v2 newly makes theoretical recovery of the posterior conditional distribution a central contribution and extends the framework's claimed subsumption of prior methods to SVDD. The original contributions concerning three TreeG variants, non-differentiable guidance, and inference-time scaling remain. The music and DNA improvement percentages promoted into the abstract were already reported in v1.

C2.justification: v2 distinguishes resampling's theoretical role from ranking's empirical advantage. Appendix B adds a concrete limitation involving expensive, non-differentiable objectives without effective surrogate predictors. Appendix G.1.1 also explains TDS's speed-versus-effectiveness tradeoff through surrogate guidance. The earlier predictor-accuracy and predictor-latency discussion is largely retained.

D1.justification: Appendix F adds a planned code-release repository, without establishing that code is already available. It newly specifies shared predictors across training-free molecule methods, learning the regression scale, and continuing generation until the required valid-unique count is reached. Added baseline configurations are documented, while hardware and most existing music implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and Appendix A substantially broaden positioning around sequential Monte Carlo, soft-value guidance, inference-time alignment, and diffusion fine-tuning. Added discussions include Li et al. (2024), Wu et al. (2023), and Singhal et al. (2025). Appendix E.1 extends the existing SCG relationship to SVDD and emphasizes destination-state exploration as the distinguishing contribution.

P1.justification: The introduction, preliminaries, and method narrative are extensively rewritten. Related work becomes a separate early section; computational analysis moves into experimental configuration analysis; gradient-module details move to the appendix; and the appendix organization is rebuilt around proofs, algorithmic details, experiments, and limitations. These changes substantially alter the document's narrative structure.

P2.justification: The main text switches from two columns to one. Figure 1 adds a separate gradient-guidance schematic, Figure 2 changes its molecular objective and removes baseline markers, and result tables are rebuilt around additional methods and diversity metrics. The full music scaling table and ring-count histograms disappear, while DNA scaling figures are consolidated and supplemented with additional views.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens empirical assessment through additional baselines, molecular objectives, diversity measurements, and the selection ablation. However, it removes validity reporting and detailed scaling uncertainties. Its new theoretical guarantees also have a substantive problem: Appendix D.4, Lemma 2(b), asserts vanishing L1 error between a finite empirical law and a continuous target, which cannot hold as stated. The empirical gains coexist with lost transparency and new theoretical reliability concerns, preventing a confident net-quality judgment.
